1	"""The universal-journal posting engine (D-017): draft creation, two-flush posting, reversal.
2	
3	Every invariant lives at BOTH the service (here, for a clean 422) and the DB (migration 0009
4	triggers, the bypass-proof backstop). Three load-bearing mechanisms (D-017): (1) TWO-FLUSH
5	posting — the uow does not guarantee cross-table UPDATE order, so we flush the loaded lines'
6	``is_posted`` while the entry is still DRAFT (the line trigger keys on OLD.is_posted=FALSE),
7	THEN flush the header POSTED (balance + period triggers fire there); (2) LOADED-object mutation,
8	never bulk ``update()``, so audit diffs are captured and the audit bulk-write assertion holds
9	(D-010); (3) REVERSAL-only correction — a posted entry is never edited/deleted, only reversed.
10	
11	For v1 functional amounts EQUAL transaction amounts (single functional currency; FX in 4.3). The
12	balance check sums functional amounts, exact on both engines (MoneyType stores NUMERIC / micro-unit
13	ints, D-015).
14	"""
15	
16	from __future__ import annotations
17	
18	import uuid
19	from datetime import UTC, date, datetime
20	from decimal import Decimal
21	
22	from sqlalchemy import select
23	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
24	
25	from app.core import docflow
26	from app.core.events import publish
27	from app.core.exceptions import ConflictError, ValidationFailedError
28	from app.core.numbering import claim_number, ensure_sequence
29	from app.modules.finance import queries
30	from app.modules.finance.constants import (
31	    JOURNAL_ENTRY_DOC_TYPE,
32	    JOURNAL_NUMBER_PADDING,
33	    JOURNAL_NUMBER_PREFIX,
34	    JOURNAL_SEQUENCE_NAME,
35	    DocumentType,
36	    EntryStatus,
37	    PeriodStatus,
38	)
39	from app.modules.finance.events import JournalEntryPosted, JournalEntryReversed
40	from app.modules.finance.models import Account, JournalEntry, JournalLine
41	from app.modules.finance.schemas import JournalEntryCreate, JournalLineCreate
42	from app.modules.finance.service.journal_read import (
43	    entry_totals,
44	    get_entry,
45	    load_lines,
46	)
47	
48	# core/docflow link type for the reverses-edge (D-012 vocabulary).
49	_REVERSES_LINK = "reverses"
50	
51	
52	def _assert_line_one_sided(payload: JournalLineCreate, line_number: int) -> None:
53	    debit = payload.transaction_debit_amount
54	    credit = payload.transaction_credit_amount
55	    one_sided = (debit > 0 and credit == 0) or (credit > 0 and debit == 0)
56	    if not one_sided:
57	        raise ValidationFailedError(
58	            message=(
59	                f"Line {line_number} must have exactly one of debit/credit positive "
60	                "(the other zero)"
61	            ),
62	            code="finance.journal_line_not_one_sided",
63	            details={"line_number": line_number},
64	        )
65	
66	
67	async def _require_postable_accounts(
68	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, account_ids: set[uuid.UUID]
69	) -> None:
70	    """Every referenced account must exist in this tenant AND be postable (leaf). One query."""
71	    rows = (
72	        await session.execute(
73	            select(Account.id, Account.is_postable).where(
74	                Account.tenant_id == tenant_id, Account.id.in_(account_ids)
75	            )
76	        )
77	    ).all()
78	    found = {row[0]: row[1] for row in rows}
79	    missing = [str(aid) for aid in account_ids if aid not in found]
80	    if missing:
81	        raise ValidationFailedError(
82	            message="One or more lines reference an unknown account",
83	            code="finance.journal_account_not_found",
84	            details={"account_ids": missing},
85	        )
86	    not_postable = [str(aid) for aid, postable in found.items() if not postable]
87	    if not_postable:
88	        raise ValidationFailedError(
89	            message="One or more lines reference a non-postable account",
90	            code="finance.journal_account_not_postable",
91	            details={"account_ids": not_postable},
92	        )
93	
94	
95	async def create_draft_entry(
96	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: JournalEntryCreate
97	) -> JournalEntry:
98	    """Create a DRAFT entry + lines (D-017). Validates: >= 2 lines, each one-sided, all accounts
99	    exist + postable + same tenant, and the entry balances (sum debits == sum credits). Registers
100	    the document in core_documents with NO number (claimed at posting per D-012). Sets functional
101	    == transaction for now (single functional currency, FX in 4.3). Does NOT claim a number and
102	    does NOT resolve the period — both happen at posting."""
103	    if len(payload.lines) < 2:
104	        raise ValidationFailedError(
105	            message="A journal entry needs at least two lines",
106	            code="finance.journal_too_few_lines",
107	        )
108	
109	    total_debit = Decimal(0)
110	    total_credit = Decimal(0)
111	    for index, line in enumerate(payload.lines, start=1):
112	        _assert_line_one_sided(line, index)
113	        total_debit += line.transaction_debit_amount
114	        total_credit += line.transaction_credit_amount
115	    if total_debit != total_credit:
116	        raise ValidationFailedError(
117	            message="Journal entry debits and credits must balance",
118	            code="finance.journal_unbalanced",
119	            details={"total_debit": str(total_debit), "total_credit": str(total_credit)},
120	        )
121	
122	    account_ids = {line.account_id for line in payload.lines}
123	    await _require_postable_accounts(session, tenant_id, account_ids)
124	
125	    entry_id = uuid.uuid4()
126	    document = await docflow.register_document(
127	        session,
128	        tenant_id,
129	        JOURNAL_ENTRY_DOC_TYPE,
130	        entry_id,
131	        doc_number=None,
132	        status=EntryStatus.DRAFT.value,
133	    )
134	    entry = JournalEntry(
135	        id=entry_id,
136	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
137	        document_id=document.id,
138	        posting_date=payload.posting_date,
139	        currency_code=payload.currency_code,
140	        description=payload.description,
141	        document_type=DocumentType(payload.document_type).value,
142	        status=EntryStatus.DRAFT.value,
143	    )
144	    session.add(entry)
145	    for index, line in enumerate(payload.lines, start=1):
146	        session.add(
147	            JournalLine(
148	                tenant_id=tenant_id,
149	                journal_entry_id=entry_id,
150	                line_number=index,
151	                account_id=line.account_id,
152	                description=line.description,
153	                transaction_debit_amount=line.transaction_debit_amount,
154	                transaction_credit_amount=line.transaction_credit_amount,
155	                # v1: functional == transaction (FX translation in 4.3).
156	                functional_debit_amount=line.transaction_debit_amount,
157	                functional_credit_amount=line.transaction_credit_amount,
158	                currency_code=payload.currency_code,
159	                cost_center_id=line.cost_center_id,
160	                profit_center_id=line.profit_center_id,
161	                project_id=line.project_id,
162	                item_id=line.item_id,
163	                partner_type=line.partner_type,
164	                partner_id=line.partner_id,
165	            )
166	        )
167	    await session.flush()
168	    return entry
169	
170	
171	async def post_entry(
172	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, entry_id: uuid.UUID
173	) -> JournalEntry:
174	    """THE posting protocol (D-017 two-flush). Validates DRAFT + balanced, resolves + checks the
175	    open period from posting_date (422 before touching the DB), claims the gapless number in this
176	    transaction, then flushes the loaded lines (still DRAFT) and finally the POSTED header (balance
177	    + period triggers fire there). Publishes JournalEntryPosted; the caller commits via uow."""
178	    entry = await get_entry(session, tenant_id, entry_id)
179	    if entry.status != EntryStatus.DRAFT.value:
180	        raise ConflictError(
181	            message="Only a draft journal entry can be posted",
182	            code="finance.journal_not_draft",
183	            details={"status": entry.status},
184	        )
185	
186	    lines = await load_lines(session, tenant_id, entry_id)
187	    if len(lines) < 2:
188	        raise ValidationFailedError(
189	            message="A journal entry needs at least two lines",
190	            code="finance.journal_too_few_lines",
191	        )
192	    debit, credit = entry_totals(lines)
193	    if debit != credit or debit <= 0:
194	        raise ValidationFailedError(
195	            message="Journal entry debits and credits must balance and be positive",
196	            code="finance.journal_unbalanced",
197	            details={"total_debit": str(debit), "total_credit": str(credit)},
198	        )
199	
200	    # Period resolution + open check FIRST (service-level half of D-018); the trigger backstops.
201	    period = await queries.find_period_for_date(session, tenant_id, entry.posting_date)
202	    if period is None or period.status != PeriodStatus.OPEN.value:
203	        raise ValidationFailedError(
204	            message="The posting date is not within an open fiscal period",
205	            code="finance.period_closed",
206	            details={"posting_date": entry.posting_date.isoformat()},
207	        )
208	
209	    # Claim the gapless number in this transaction (D-012): gapless because the claim and the
210	    # POSTED commit succeed or roll back together.
211	    await ensure_sequence(
212	        session,
213	        tenant_id,
214	        JOURNAL_SEQUENCE_NAME,
215	        JOURNAL_NUMBER_PREFIX,
216	        JOURNAL_NUMBER_PADDING,
217	        year_reset=True,
218	    )
219	    entry_number = await claim_number(
220	        session, tenant_id, JOURNAL_SEQUENCE_NAME, on_date=entry.posting_date
221	    )
222	
223	    # Flush 1: denormalize onto the loaded lines while the entry is still DRAFT.
224	    for line in lines:
225	        line.is_posted = True
226	        line.posting_date = entry.posting_date
227	        line.fiscal_period_id = period.id
228	    await session.flush()
229	
230	    # Flush 2: promote the header. The period + balance triggers fire on this DRAFT->POSTED UPDATE.
231	    entry.entry_number = entry_number
232	    entry.fiscal_period_id = period.id
233	    entry.status = EntryStatus.POSTED.value
234	    entry.posted_at = datetime.now(UTC)
235	    await session.flush()
236	
237	    await docflow.set_document_status(
238	        session,
239	        tenant_id,
240	        entry.document_id,
241	        status=EntryStatus.POSTED.value,
242	        doc_number=entry_number,
243	    )
244	
245	    publish(
246	        session,
247	        JournalEntryPosted(
248	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
249	            entry_id=entry.id,
250	            entry_number=entry_number,
251	            document_type=entry.document_type,
252	            posting_date=entry.posting_date.isoformat(),
253	            currency_code=entry.currency_code,
254	            total_functional_amount=debit,
255	            account_ids=tuple(line.account_id for line in lines),
256	        ),
257	    )
258	    return entry
259	
260	
261	async def reverse_entry(
262	    session: AsyncSession,
263	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
264	    entry_id: uuid.UUID,
265	    reversal_date: date,
266	    description: str | None = None,
267	) -> JournalEntry:
268	    """Reverse a POSTED entry (D-017). Creates a NEW same-document_type entry with each line's
269	    debit/credit SWAPPED, posts it into ``reversal_date``'s open period (its own number), then
270	    sets the original REVERSED + reversed_by_entry_id — the ONLY mutation the immutability trigger
271	    permits. Links the two documents ('reverses'), publishes JournalEntryReversed, returns the
272	    reversing entry."""
273	    original = await get_entry(session, tenant_id, entry_id)
274	    if original.status != EntryStatus.POSTED.value:
275	        raise ConflictError(
276	            message="Only a posted journal entry can be reversed",
277	            code="finance.journal_not_posted",
278	            details={"status": original.status},
279	        )
280	    if original.reversed_by_entry_id is not None:
281	        raise ConflictError(
282	            message="This journal entry has already been reversed",
283	            code="finance.journal_already_reversed",
284	        )
285	
286	    original_lines = await load_lines(session, tenant_id, entry_id)
287	
288	    reversal_id = uuid.uuid4()
289	    reversal_document = await docflow.register_document(
290	        session,
291	        tenant_id,
292	        JOURNAL_ENTRY_DOC_TYPE,
293	        reversal_id,
294	        doc_number=None,
295	        status=EntryStatus.DRAFT.value,
296	    )
297	    reversal = JournalEntry(
298	        id=reversal_id,
299	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
300	        document_id=reversal_document.id,
301	        posting_date=reversal_date,
302	        currency_code=original.currency_code,
303	        description=description
304	        or f"Reversal of {original.entry_number or original.id}",
305	        document_type=original.document_type,
306	        status=EntryStatus.DRAFT.value,
307	        reverses_entry_id=original.id,
308	    )
309	    session.add(reversal)
310	    for line in original_lines:
311	        session.add(
312	            JournalLine(
313	                tenant_id=tenant_id,
314	                journal_entry_id=reversal_id,
315	                line_number=line.line_number,
316	                account_id=line.account_id,
317	                description=line.description,
318	                # Swap debit <-> credit in both currency pairs (frozen functional amounts).
319	                transaction_debit_amount=line.transaction_credit_amount,
320	                transaction_credit_amount=line.transaction_debit_amount,
321	                functional_debit_amount=line.functional_credit_amount,
322	                functional_credit_amount=line.functional_debit_amount,
323	                currency_code=line.currency_code,
324	                cost_center_id=line.cost_center_id,
325	                profit_center_id=line.profit_center_id,
326	                project_id=line.project_id,
327	                item_id=line.item_id,
328	                partner_type=line.partner_type,
329	                partner_id=line.partner_id,
330	            )
331	        )
332	    await session.flush()
333	
334	    # Post the reversing entry (claims its own number, runs the same period/balance checks).
335	    await post_entry(session, tenant_id, reversal_id)
336	
337	    # The single sanctioned mutation on a POSTED original (immutability trigger permits exactly
338	    # this: status POSTED->REVERSED with reversed_by_entry_id set).
339	    original.reversed_by_entry_id = reversal_id
340	    original.status = EntryStatus.REVERSED.value
341	    await session.flush()
342	
343	    await docflow.set_document_status(
344	        session, tenant_id, original.document_id, status=EntryStatus.REVERSED.value
345	    )
346	    await docflow.link_documents(
347	        session,
348	        tenant_id,
349	        predecessor=original.document_id,
350	        successor=reversal.document_id,
351	        link_type=_REVERSES_LINK,
352	    )
353	
354	    await session.refresh(reversal)
355	    publish(
356	        session,
357	        JournalEntryReversed(
358	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
359	            entry_id=original.id,
360	            reversal_entry_id=reversal.id,
361	            reversal_entry_number=reversal.entry_number or "",
362	            document_type=original.document_type,
363	            reversal_date=reversal_date.isoformat(),
364	        ),
365	    )
366	    return reversal

1	"""Finance's cross-module read interface (STRUCTURE §5).
2	
3	Finance is the bottom of the dependency order: every other module (inventory, sales, ...)
4	may import THIS file to read finance state synchronously, and finance imports no other
5	module's queries. Keep this surface thin and stable — it is a contract. The journal posting
6	flow (4.2) calls ``find_period_for_date`` to resolve an entry's period from its posting_date;
7	inventory/sales call ``get_period_status`` to refuse stock/sales documents dated into a closed
8	period before they reach the GL.
9	
10	Every function takes an explicit ``tenant_id`` and runs under the caller's tenant context, so
11	the D-007 filter applies on top of the explicit predicate — these are ordinary tenant-scoped
12	ORM reads, not a bypass.
13	"""
14	
15	import uuid
16	from datetime import date
17	
18	from sqlalchemy import select
19	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
20	
21	from app.modules.finance.constants import PeriodStatus
22	from app.modules.finance.models import Account, FiscalPeriod
23	
24	
25	async def find_period_for_date(
26	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, on_date: date
27	) -> FiscalPeriod | None:
28	    """The fiscal period whose [start_date, end_date] (inclusive) covers ``on_date``, or
29	    None if no period does. Periods within a year are contiguous and non-overlapping (the
30	    service enforces that on generation), so at most one matches. This is the date->period
31	    lookup the journal uses on every posting (4.2)."""
32	    stmt = select(FiscalPeriod).where(
33	        FiscalPeriod.tenant_id == tenant_id,
34	        FiscalPeriod.start_date <= on_date,
35	        FiscalPeriod.end_date >= on_date,
36	    )
37	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
38	
39	
40	async def get_period_status(
41	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, on_date: date
42	) -> PeriodStatus | None:
43	    """The OPEN/CLOSED status of the period covering ``on_date``, or None when no period
44	    covers it. Callers posting financial or stock documents check this up front: None or
45	    CLOSED means the date is not in an open period and the document must be rejected
46	    (the DB-level period trigger on the journal in 4.2 is the bypass-proof backstop)."""
47	    period = await find_period_for_date(session, tenant_id, on_date)
48	    if period is None:
49	        return None
50	    return PeriodStatus(period.status)
51	
52	
53	async def account_exists(
54	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, code: str
55	) -> bool:
56	    """Whether an account with ``code`` exists in the tenant's chart of accounts. Lets
57	    another module validate a referenced account code without importing finance models."""
58	    stmt = select(Account.id).where(
59	        Account.tenant_id == tenant_id, Account.code == code
60	    )
61	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).first() is not None
62

1	"""Domain events finance PUBLISHES (D-011). Declarative data only — no logic, no models — so
2	another module's ``handlers.py`` may import these typed classes (the STRUCTURE §5 events.py
3	allowance). Inventory and other modules subscribe in a later phase; the payload carries the
4	entry id plus amount/account summaries so a subscriber needs no finance read to react.
5	
6	For v1 functional amounts equal transaction amounts (single functional currency); the event
7	carries the functional total since that is what downstream ledger consumers reconcile against.
8	"""
9	
10	import uuid
11	from decimal import Decimal
12	from typing import ClassVar
13	
14	from app.core.events import DomainEvent
15	
16	
17	class JournalEntryPosted(DomainEvent):
18	    """A draft journal entry was posted (D-017). Fired inside the posting transaction after the
19	    DRAFT->POSTED flush; a handler runs in the SAME transaction (D-011), so any cross-module
20	    effect it triggers commits or rolls back with the posting."""
21	
22	    key: ClassVar[str] = "finance.journal.posted"
23	
24	    entry_id: uuid.UUID
25	    entry_number: str
26	    document_type: str
27	    posting_date: str
28	    currency_code: str
29	    total_functional_amount: Decimal
30	    account_ids: tuple[uuid.UUID, ...]
31	
32	
33	class JournalEntryReversed(DomainEvent):
34	    """A posted entry was reversed by a new reversing entry (D-017). Carries both ids so a
35	    subscriber can mirror the correction (e.g. reverse a derived posting)."""
36

2	
3	Split out of ``service/journal.py`` so the write engine (create/post/reverse) stays under the
4	STRUCTURE §3 400-line cap; both halves are the one journal aggregate. The write engine imports the
5	loaders from here; the router imports the read functions through the ``service`` package surface.
6	"""
7	
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	import uuid
11	from decimal import Decimal
12	
13	from sqlalchemy import select
14	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
15	
16	from app.core.exceptions import NotFoundError
17	from app.core.pagination import OrderKey, SortDirection, filter_fingerprint, paginate
18	from app.core.schemas import Page

23	async def load_lines(

27	    stmt = (
28	        select(JournalLine)
29	        .where(
30	            JournalLine.tenant_id == tenant_id,
31	            JournalLine.journal_entry_id == entry_id,
32	        )
33	        .order_by(JournalLine.line_number)
34	    )

60	    """(total functional debit, total functional credit) over the lines — the balance check
61	    operand. MoneyType result values are Decimal, so the sum is exact (D-015)."""
62	    debit = sum((line.functional_debit_amount for line in lines), Decimal(0))

1	"""Fiscal year/period business logic and the open/close lifecycle (D-018).
2	
3	- ``create_fiscal_year`` generates ``period_count`` contiguous, non-overlapping monthly
4	  periods (D-018); the generated periods exactly tile the year.
5	- period lifecycle: ``close_period`` / ``open_period`` flip a period's status; the
6	  "cannot close a period while unposted drafts exist in it" rule and the DB-level
7	  posting-rejection trigger arrive with the journal (4.2) — see ``assert_period_closable``
8	  for the clearly-marked seam. ``close_fiscal_year`` requires all the year's periods closed.
9	"""
10	
11	import calendar
12	import uuid
13	from datetime import date, timedelta
14	
15	from sqlalchemy import select
16	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
17	
18	from app.core.exceptions import ConflictError, NotFoundError, ValidationFailedError
19	from app.modules.finance.constants import EntryStatus, PeriodStatus
20	from app.modules.finance.models import FiscalPeriod, FiscalYear, JournalEntry
21	from app.modules.finance.schemas import FiscalYearCreate
22	
23	
24	def _add_months(anchor: date, months: int) -> date:
25	    """``anchor`` shifted forward by ``months`` calendar months, clamped to the target
26	    month's last valid day (so 2026-01-31 + 1 month = 2026-02-28). Used to walk monthly
27	    period boundaries without an external date library."""
28	    total = anchor.month - 1 + months
29	    year = anchor.year + total // 12
30	    month = total % 12 + 1
31	    last_day = calendar.monthrange(year, month)[1]
32	    return date(year, month, min(anchor.day, last_day))
33	
34	
35	def generate_periods(start_date: date, period_count: int) -> list[tuple[int, date, date]]:
36	    """Build ``period_count`` contiguous, non-overlapping monthly period boundaries from
37	    ``start_date`` (D-018). Returns ``(period_number, start, end)`` tuples where each period
38	    runs from its start to the day before the next period's start, so the periods exactly
39	    tile [start_date, last period end] with no gaps and no overlaps."""
40	    if period_count < 1:
41	        raise ValidationFailedError(
42	            message="A fiscal year needs at least one period",
43	            code="finance.invalid_period_count",
44	        )
45	    boundaries: list[tuple[int, date, date]] = []
46	    period_start = start_date
47	    for number in range(1, period_count + 1):
48	        next_start = _add_months(start_date, number)
49	        period_end = next_start - timedelta(days=1)
50	        boundaries.append((number, period_start, period_end))
51	        period_start = next_start
52	    return boundaries
53	
54	
55	async def create_fiscal_year(
56	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: FiscalYearCreate
57	) -> FiscalYear:
58	    """Create a fiscal year and auto-generate its monthly periods (D-018). The year's
59	    end_date is set to the last generated period's end so the periods exactly tile the year.
60	    All periods (and the year) start OPEN. Rejects a duplicate year code with a ConflictError."""
61	    existing = (
62	        await session.execute(
63	            select(FiscalYear).where(
64	                FiscalYear.tenant_id == tenant_id, FiscalYear.code == payload.code
65	            )
66	        )
67	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
68	    if existing is not None:
69	        raise ConflictError(
70	            message=f"A fiscal year with code {payload.code} already exists",
71	            code="finance.fiscal_year_code_conflict",
72	            details={"code": payload.code},
73	        )
74	
75	    boundaries = generate_periods(payload.start_date, payload.period_count)
76	    year_end = boundaries[-1][2]
77	    year = FiscalYear(
78	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
79	        code=payload.code,
80	        name=payload.name,
81	        start_date=payload.start_date,
82	        end_date=year_end,
83	        status=PeriodStatus.OPEN.value,
84	    )
85	    session.add(year)
86	    await session.flush()  # year.id needed for the period FKs below
87	
88	    for number, period_start, period_end in boundaries:
89	        session.add(
90	            FiscalPeriod(
91	                tenant_id=tenant_id,
92	                fiscal_year_id=year.id,
93	                period_number=number,
94	                name=f"{payload.code}-{number:02d}",
95	                start_date=period_start,
96	                end_date=period_end,
97	                status=PeriodStatus.OPEN.value,
98	            )
99	        )
100	    await session.flush()
101	    return year
102	
103	
104	async def list_fiscal_years(session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID) -> list[FiscalYear]:
105	    stmt = (
106	        select(FiscalYear)
107	        .where(FiscalYear.tenant_id == tenant_id)
108	        .order_by(FiscalYear.start_date)
109	    )
110	    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())
111	
112	
113	async def list_fiscal_periods(
114	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, fiscal_year_id: uuid.UUID | None = None
115	) -> list[FiscalPeriod]:
116	    stmt = select(FiscalPeriod).where(FiscalPeriod.tenant_id == tenant_id)
117	    if fiscal_year_id is not None:
118	        stmt = stmt.where(FiscalPeriod.fiscal_year_id == fiscal_year_id)
119	    stmt = stmt.order_by(FiscalPeriod.start_date)
120	    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())
121	
122	
123	async def _require_period(
124	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, period_id: uuid.UUID
125	) -> FiscalPeriod:
126	    period = await session.get(FiscalPeriod, period_id)
127	    if period is None or period.tenant_id != tenant_id:
128	        raise NotFoundError(
129	            message="Fiscal period not found", code="finance.fiscal_period_not_found"
130	        )
131	    return period
132	
133	
134	async def assert_period_closable(
135	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, period: FiscalPeriod
136	) -> None:
137	    """The close-time invariant (D-018): a period may close only if it is not already closed
138	    AND it holds no DRAFT journal entries dated within it.
139	
140	    Closing a period asserts it is settled; a DRAFT entry dated inside it is unfinished work
141	    that would become unpostable (the period trigger would then reject its posting). So we
142	    refuse the close until every draft in the period is posted or removed. Posted/reversed
143	    entries are fine — they are immutable settled facts. This is the service-level half of
144	    D-018; the DB-level period-posting trigger on ``fin_journal_entries`` is the bypass-proof
145	    backstop for postings themselves.
146	    """
147	    if period.status == PeriodStatus.CLOSED.value:
148	        raise ValidationFailedError(
149	            message="Fiscal period is already closed",
150	            code="finance.period_already_closed",
151	        )
152	    draft_in_period = (
153	        await session.execute(
154	            select(JournalEntry.id).where(
155	                JournalEntry.tenant_id == tenant_id,
156	                JournalEntry.status == EntryStatus.DRAFT.value,
157	                JournalEntry.posting_date >= period.start_date,
158	                JournalEntry.posting_date <= period.end_date,
159	            )
160	        )
161	    ).first()
162	    if draft_in_period is not None:
163	        raise ValidationFailedError(
164	            message="Cannot close a period that contains draft journal entries",
165	            code="finance.period_has_draft_entries",
166	        )
167	
168	
169	async def close_period(
170	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, period_id: uuid.UUID
171	) -> FiscalPeriod:
172	    """Close a fiscal period (D-018). Runs the closable check (the journal seam above) then
173	    sets status CLOSED. Once the journal exists, postings dated into this period are rejected
174	    at both the service and DB level."""
175	    period = await _require_period(session, tenant_id, period_id)
176	    await assert_period_closable(session, tenant_id, period)
177	    period.status = PeriodStatus.CLOSED.value
178	    await session.flush()
179	    return period
180	
181	
182	async def open_period(
183	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, period_id: uuid.UUID
184	) -> FiscalPeriod:
185	    """Reopen a closed fiscal period (D-018). Reopening a period whose year is already CLOSED
186	    is refused — a closed year asserts every period in it is settled."""
187	    period = await _require_period(session, tenant_id, period_id)
188	    year = await session.get(FiscalYear, period.fiscal_year_id)
189	    if year is not None and year.status == PeriodStatus.CLOSED.value:
190	        raise ValidationFailedError(
191	            message="Cannot reopen a period whose fiscal year is closed",
192	            code="finance.fiscal_year_closed",
193	        )
194	    period.status = PeriodStatus.OPEN.value
195	    await session.flush()
196	    return period
197	
198	
199	async def close_fiscal_year(
200	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, fiscal_year_id: uuid.UUID
201	) -> FiscalYear:
202	    """Close a fiscal year, allowed only once every one of its periods is CLOSED (D-018) — a
203	    closed year is the assertion that the whole year is settled."""
204	    year = await session.get(FiscalYear, fiscal_year_id)
205	    if year is None or year.tenant_id != tenant_id:
206	        raise NotFoundError(
207	            message="Fiscal year not found", code="finance.fiscal_year_not_found"
208	        )
209	    open_periods = (
210	        await session.execute(
211	            select(FiscalPeriod.id).where(
212	                FiscalPeriod.tenant_id == tenant_id,
213	                FiscalPeriod.fiscal_year_id == fiscal_year_id,
214	                FiscalPeriod.status == PeriodStatus.OPEN.value,
215	            )
216	        )
217	    ).first()
218	    if open_periods is not None:
219	        raise ValidationFailedError(
220	            message="Cannot close a fiscal year while any of its periods is open",
221	            code="finance.fiscal_year_has_open_periods",
222	        )
223	    year.status = PeriodStatus.CLOSED.value
224	    await session.flush()
225	    return year

59	async def _commit[T](session: SessionDep, work: Callable[[], Awaitable[T]]) -> T:
60	    """Run a service call inside the D-011 uow and return its ORM result (captured in a one-slot
61	    holder since ``run_in_uow`` returns None). The result is refreshed inside the work so server
62	    defaults/``onupdate`` columns materialize in the async context — else the caller's sync

64	    holder: list[T] = []

67	        result = await work()
68	        await session.refresh(result)
69	        holder.append(result)
70	
71	    await run_in_uow(session, _work)
72	    return holder[0]

270	        session, lambda: service.open_period(session, current.tenant_id, period_id)
271	    )
272	    return FiscalPeriodRead.model_validate(period)

278	async def _entry_detail(
279	    session: SessionDep, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, entry_id: uuid.UUID
280	) -> JournalEntryDetail:
281	    """Load an entry + its lines into the detail schema. ``refresh`` materializes the server-side
282	    ``updated_at`` in the async context before the sync ``model_validate`` (else an expired
283	    attribute triggers an async lazy-load in sync serialization — MissingGreenlet)."""
284	    entry, lines = await service.get_entry_with_lines(session, tenant_id, entry_id)
285	    await session.refresh(entry)
286	    header = JournalEntryRead.model_validate(entry)
287	    return JournalEntryDetail(
288	        **header.model_dump(),
289	        lines=[JournalLineRead.model_validate(line) for line in lines],
290	    )

295	    response_model=JournalEntryRead,

301	    current: CurrentUserDep,
302	    session: SessionDep,
303	) -> JournalEntryRead:
304	    """Create a DRAFT entry (no number claimed). journal.post covers create + post."""
305	    entry = await _commit(
306	        session, lambda: service.create_draft_entry(session, current.tenant_id, payload)
307	    )
308	    return JournalEntryRead.model_validate(entry)

311	@router.post(
312	    "/journal-entries/{entry_id}/post",
313	    response_model=JournalEntryDetail,
314	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(FINANCE_JOURNAL_POST))],
315	)
316	async def post_journal_entry(
317	    entry_id: uuid.UUID,
318	    current: CurrentUserDep,
319	    session: SessionDep,
320	    idem: IdempotentDep = _PostIdempotentDep,
321	) -> JournalEntryDetail:
322	    """Post a draft entry (D-017). IDEMPOTENT (D-013): capture() lands in the posting uow, so the
323	    document and the replay record commit atomically."""
324	    holder: dict[str, JournalEntryDetail] = {}
325	
326	    async def work() -> None:
327	        await service.post_entry(session, current.tenant_id, entry_id)
328	        detail = await _entry_detail(session, current.tenant_id, entry_id)
329	        holder["read"] = await idem.capture(detail)
330	
331	    await run_in_uow(session, work)
332	    return holder["read"]

336	    "/journal-entries/{entry_id}/reverse",
337	    response_model=JournalEntryDetail,
338	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(FINANCE_JOURNAL_REVERSE))],
339	)

341	    entry_id: uuid.UUID,
342	    payload: JournalEntryReverseRequest,
343	    current: CurrentUserDep,
344	    session: SessionDep,
345	    idem: IdempotentDep = _ReverseIdempotentDep,
346	) -> JournalEntryDetail:
347	    """Reverse a posted entry (D-017); returns the NEW reversing entry with lines. IDEMPOTENT."""
348	    holder: dict[str, JournalEntryDetail] = {}
349	
350	    async def work() -> None:
351	        reversal = await service.reverse_entry(
352	            session,
353	            current.tenant_id,
354	            entry_id,
355	            payload.reversal_date,
356	            payload.description,
357	        )
358	        detail = await _entry_detail(session, current.tenant_id, reversal.id)
359	        holder["read"] = await idem.capture(detail)
360	
361	    await run_in_uow(session, work)
362	    return holder["read"]

5	string, matching how the columns store them). Create/Update carry only the client-settable

1	"""Declarative Base with the D-022 naming convention and shared model mixins."""
2	
3	import uuid
4	from datetime import datetime
5	from typing import Any
6	
7	import sqlalchemy as sa
8	from sqlalchemy.dialects import postgresql
9	from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, declared_attr, mapped_column
10	
11	# Deterministic constraint names are mandatory: SQLite batch-mode migrations
12	# cannot drop unnamed constraints (D-022).
13	NAMING_CONVENTION = {
14	    "ix": "ix_%(column_0_label)s",
15	    "uq": "uq_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s",
16	    "ck": "ck_%(table_name)s_%(constraint_name)s",
17	    "fk": "fk_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s_%(referred_table_name)s",
18	    "pk": "pk_%(table_name)s",
19	}
20	
21	# Portable JSON: JSONB on Postgres, plain JSON elsewhere. Type variance lives in
22	# the models so migrations import it from here and stay dialect-clean (D-022).
23	JSON_VARIANT = sa.JSON().with_variant(postgresql.JSONB(), "postgresql")
24	
25	
26	class Base(DeclarativeBase):
27	    metadata = sa.MetaData(naming_convention=NAMING_CONVENTION)
28	
29	
30	class UuidPKMixin:
31	    """uuid4 primary key, client-generated so ids are portable across both engines."""
32	
33	    id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4)
34	
35	
36	class TenantMixin:
37	    """Row-level tenancy marker (D-007). Filtering and stamping are enforced by the
38	    core/tenancy.py session listeners; query authors never touch tenant_id."""
39	
40	    @declared_attr
41	    def tenant_id(cls) -> Mapped[uuid.UUID]:
42	        return mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False, index=True)
43	
44	
45	class AuditMixin:
46	    """Marker mixin (D-010): tags a model for split-phase audit capture. It adds NO
47	    columns — the audit listeners in core/audit.py test ``isinstance(obj, AuditMixin)``
48	    to decide which INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE flushes land in core_audit_log. Per-column
49	    opt-outs are declared on the model via ``__audit_exclude__`` (a frozenset of
50	    attribute names); ``password_hash`` is excluded there on User."""
51	
52	    # Attribute names never written to the diff (D-010: password_hash always). Models
53	    # override by setting their own frozenset; the listeners read it via getattr.
54	    __audit_exclude__: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
55	
56	
57	class TimestampMixin:
58	    """Timezone-aware UTC stamps with server-side defaults on both engines."""
59	
60	    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
61	        sa.DateTime(timezone=True),
62	        nullable=False,
63	        server_default=sa.func.now(),
64	    )
65	    updated_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
66	        sa.DateTime(timezone=True),
67	        nullable=False,
68	        server_default=sa.func.now(),
69	        onupdate=sa.func.now(),
70	    )
71	
72	
73	def tenant_fk(target_table: str, local_column: str | None = None) -> sa.ForeignKeyConstraint:
74	    """Tenant-safe foreign key for __table_args__ (D-007 item 4).
75	
76	    - tenant_fk("adm_tenants") anchors tenant_id itself to the tenants root;
77	      every tenant-scoped table carries this backstop.
78	    - tenant_fk("inv_items", "item_id") builds the composite (tenant_id, item_id)
79	      -> (inv_items.tenant_id, inv_items.id) FK, so a child row can never point
80	      at a parent row of another tenant; the parent declares tenant_unique().
81	    """
82	    if local_column is None:
83	        return sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(["tenant_id"], [f"{target_table}.id"])
84	    return sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
85	        ["tenant_id", local_column],
86	        [f"{target_table}.tenant_id", f"{target_table}.id"],
87	    )
88	
89	
90	def tenant_unique() -> sa.UniqueConstraint:
91	    """UNIQUE (tenant_id, id) — required on every tenant-scoped table that is
92	    referenced through tenant_fk() composite FKs (D-007 item 4). Any OTHER unique
93	    constraint starting with tenant_id needs an explicit name at the call site:
94	    the D-022 naming convention keys on column 0 only and would collide."""
95	    return sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "id")
96	
97	
98	class User(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
99	    """Auth principal (D-008). Cross-cutting platform entity, so it lives in core
100	    (STRUCTURE §2 litmus: users are not a business concept). Provisioning is owned
101	    by modules/admin (PLAN 14); login lookup runs under system_context (D-007 site 1).
102	    HR compensation/PII masking is HR's concern later — these rows are credentials only.
103	    Audited (D-010): security-relevant; password_hash is excluded from every diff."""
104	
105	    __tablename__ = "core_users"
106	    # D-010: never write the credential into the audit diff (insert, update, or delete).
107	    __audit_exclude__ = frozenset({"password_hash"})
108	    __table_args__ = (
109	        # Explicit uq name: the D-022 convention keys on column 0 (tenant_id) only and
110	        # would collide with tenant_unique() below.
111	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "email", name="uq_core_users_tenant_id_email"),
112	        tenant_unique(),
113	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
114	    )
115	
116	    email: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(320), nullable=False)
117	    password_hash: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(255), nullable=False)
118	    full_name: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), nullable=True)
119	    is_active: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
120	        sa.Boolean, nullable=False, default=True, server_default=sa.true()
121	    )
122	    # "Revoke everything" valve: bump this and every outstanding access token whose
123	    # `ver` claim no longer matches is rejected on its next request (D-008).
124	    token_version: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
125	        sa.Integer, nullable=False, default=0, server_default=sa.text("0")
126	    )
127	
128	
129	class RefreshSession(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
130	    """Refresh-token server state (D-008). The PK id is the `sid` claim. Rotation is a
131	    compare-and-swap on current_jti_hash; prev_jti_hash + rotated_at implement the
132	    10-second grace window for benign multi-tab refresh races."""
133	
134	    __tablename__ = "core_refresh_sessions"
135	    __table_args__ = (
136	        tenant_unique(),
137	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
138	        tenant_fk("core_users", "user_id"),
139	        # Hot read path: refresh loads by sid (PK already), logout/revoke and the
140	        # "active sessions" admin view filter by user within a tenant.
141	        sa.Index("ix_core_refresh_sessions_tenant_id_user_id", "tenant_id", "user_id"),
142	    )
143	
144	    user_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
145	    current_jti_hash: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(64), nullable=False)
146	    prev_jti_hash: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(64), nullable=True)
147	    rotated_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(
148	        sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=True
149	    )
150	    issued_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False)
151	    last_used_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False)
152	    expires_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False)
153	    revoked_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(
154	        sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=True
155	    )
156	    ip: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(45), nullable=True)
157	    user_agent: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(400), nullable=True)
158	
159	
160	class Permission(UuidPKMixin, Base):
161	    """Code-defined permission catalog (D-009). Deliberately NOT TenantMixin: a
162	    permission describes what the code enforces and is identical for every tenant, so
163	    one global row per key avoids N per-tenant copies and orphan keys nothing checks.
164	    Rows are upserted by core/rbac.sync_permission_catalog from the code registry —
165	    tenants can only be granted keys that already exist here."""
166	
167	    __tablename__ = "core_permissions"
168	
169	    key: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(150), nullable=False, unique=True)

1	"""D-012 document registry, flow links, and chain traversal.
2	
3	The registry turns the polymorphic (doc_type, doc_id) problem into ordinary FK integrity:
4	every business document row links to exactly one ``core_documents`` registry entry via the
5	NOT NULL ``document_id`` FK supplied by ``DocumentMixin``. Predecessor/successor edges live
6	in ``core_doc_links``, so chain traversal is one generic recursive CTE over two narrow
7	tables — the ACDOCA-era Document Relationship Browser shape — with zero module-aware code in
8	core (core imports nothing from modules).
9	
10	Claim-timing (D-012): a document is registered with ``doc_number`` NULL at creation;
11	documents with a draft lifecycle are numbered at posting via the numbering claim, documents
12	permanent at creation are numbered immediately. The partial unique index on
13	``(tenant_id, doc_number)`` is the DB backstop turning any numbering bug into a constraint
14	violation.
15	
16	The ORM models live HERE rather than in core/models.py: models.py is near its ~350-line
17	soft cap, so the D-012 entities sit in their concern file (consistent with numbering.py and
18	sanctioned by the PLAN). Noted in DECISIONS.md.
19	"""

277	def _build_reachability_cte(
278	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID, start: uuid.UUID, *, forward: bool
279	) -> sa.sql.Selectable:
280	    """One recursive CTE collecting every document reachable from ``start`` in ONE direction.
281	
282	    ``forward=True`` walks successor edges (descendants), ``forward=False`` walks predecessor
283	    edges (ancestors). The recursive member carries a ``depth`` column capped at
284	    _MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH and a ``path`` string of visited ids; the join excludes any node already
285	    on the path, so a diamond or cycle is traversed once and terminates (D-012 visited-path
286	    guard). Works identically on Postgres and SQLite (both support WITH RECURSIVE).
287	    """
288	    links = DocumentLink.__table__
289	    near = links.c.successor_document_id if forward else links.c.predecessor_document_id
290	    far = links.c.predecessor_document_id if forward else links.c.successor_document_id
291	
292	    # Anchor: the start node itself at depth 0. The path representation MUST match how the
293	    # recursive step casts ids (CAST(<Uuid column> AS VARCHAR)), so the start id is cast the
294	    # same way — casting a Uuid-typed literal renders dashless hex on SQLite and dashed on
295	    # PG, exactly as the column cast does, keeping the visited-path guard's LIKE comparison
296	    # apples-to-apples on both engines (a raw str(start) would carry dashes on SQLite and
297	    # silently defeat the guard).
298	    anchor = select(
299	        sa.literal(start, type_=sa.Uuid).label("document_id"),
300	        sa.literal(0).label("depth"),
301	        sa.cast(sa.literal(start, type_=sa.Uuid), sa.String).label("path"),
302	    ).cte("reach", recursive=True)
303	
304	    # Recursive step: from each frontier node, follow edges in the chosen direction to the
305	    # node on the other end, within the tenant, skipping nodes already on the path.
306	    step = (
307	        select(
308	            far.label("document_id"),
309	            (anchor.c.depth + 1).label("depth"),
310	            (anchor.c.path + sa.literal(",") + sa.cast(far, sa.String)).label("path"),
311	        )
312	        .select_from(anchor.join(links, near == anchor.c.document_id))
313	        .where(
314	            links.c.tenant_id == tenant_id,
315	            anchor.c.depth < _MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH,
316	            anchor.c.path.notlike(sa.literal("%") + sa.cast(far, sa.String) + sa.literal("%")),
317	        )
318	    )
319	    return anchor.union_all(step)
320

322	async def get_document_chain(
323	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, document_id: uuid.UUID
324	) -> DocumentChain:
325	    """Traverse the full flow chain around ``document_id`` in BOTH directions and return its
326	    nodes + edges (D-012). Two recursive CTEs (ancestors via predecessor edges, descendants
327	    via successor edges) collect every reachable registry id; their union is the connected
328	    component containing the start node. Edges are the links whose BOTH endpoints fall in that
329	    set. Cycles and diamonds are handled by the per-CTE visited-path guard, so each node and
330	    edge appears once. Returns empty nodes/edges when the id is unknown to this tenant.
331	
332	    Tenant isolation: the CTEs filter links by tenant_id and the registry/edge reads run
333	    under the caller's tenant context (the D-007 ORM filter), so a chain query never returns
334	    another tenant's documents.
335	    """
336	    ancestors = _build_reachability_cte(tenant_id, document_id, forward=False)
337	    descendants = _build_reachability_cte(tenant_id, document_id, forward=True)
338	
339	    ancestor_ids = set(
340	        (await session.execute(select(ancestors.c.document_id))).scalars().all()
341	    )
342	    descendant_ids = set(
343	        (await session.execute(select(descendants.c.document_id))).scalars().all()
344	    )
345	    reachable = ancestor_ids | descendant_ids
346	
347	    # An unknown id reaches only itself; if it is not a real registry row for this tenant,
348	    # there are no nodes to return — surface an empty chain (the router maps that to 404).
349	    document_rows = (
350	        await session.execute(select(Document).where(Document.id.in_(reachable)))
351	    ).scalars().all()
352	    if not document_rows:
353	        return DocumentChain(nodes=[], edges=[])
354	
355	    present_ids = {row.id for row in document_rows}
356	    nodes = [
357	        ChainNode(
358	            document_id=row.id,
359	            doc_type=row.doc_type,
360	            doc_id=row.doc_id,
361	            doc_number=row.doc_number,
362	            status=row.status,
363	        )
364	        for row in document_rows
365	    ]
366	
367	    link_rows = (
368	        await session.execute(
369	            select(DocumentLink).where(
370	                DocumentLink.predecessor_document_id.in_(present_ids),
371	                DocumentLink.successor_document_id.in_(present_ids),
372	            )
373	        )
374	    ).scalars().all()
375	    edges = [
376	        ChainEdge(
377	            predecessor_document_id=link.predecessor_document_id,

1	"""RBAC engine (D-009): code-defined permission catalog, permission resolution with a
2	short TTL cache, the require_permission dependency factory, and field-level read masking.
3	
4	The catalog is the source of truth: modules declare their permission keys in their
5	``constants.py`` and register them here at import time via ``register_permissions``;
6	``sync_permission_catalog`` upserts the registry into ``core_permissions`` so tenants
7	can only ever be granted keys that some code path actually checks. Roles and grants are
8	tenant data (core/models.py); resolution joins user_roles -> role_permissions ->
9	permissions in one query, memoized 60s keyed on (tenant_id, user_id, token_version).
10	"""
11	
12	import functools
13	import time
14	import uuid
15	from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
16	from contextvars import ContextVar
17	from typing import Annotated, Any
18	
19	from fastapi import Depends
20	from pydantic import WrapSerializer
21	from pydantic_core.core_schema import SerializerFunctionWrapHandler
22	from sqlalchemy import select
23	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
24	
25	from app.core.exceptions import PermissionDeniedError
26	from app.core.models import Permission, RolePermission, UserRole
27	
28	# --- Permission catalog (code-defined source of truth) ------------------------
29	
30	# Module-level registry. Modules call register_permissions at import; the values are
31	# the human-readable descriptions seeded alongside the key. Insertion-ordered so the
32	# catalog sync and tests see a stable order.
33	_CATALOG: dict[str, str | None] = {}
34	
35	
36	def register_permissions(*keys: str, descriptions: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> None:
37	    """Declare permission keys that exist in code (D-009). Idempotent: re-registering a
38	    key keeps the first description unless a new one is supplied. Modules call this at
39	    import from their ``constants.py`` (e.g. ``register_permissions(FIN_JOURNAL_POST)``)."""
40	    descriptions = descriptions or {}
41	    for key in keys:
42	        new_description = descriptions.get(key)
43	        if key not in _CATALOG or new_description is not None:
44	            _CATALOG[key] = new_description if new_description is not None else _CATALOG.get(key)
45	
46	
47	def catalog_keys() -> frozenset[str]:
48	    """The full set of code-declared permission keys (the grantable universe)."""
49	    return frozenset(_CATALOG)
50	
51	
52	# Core permission keys, registered at import (module __init__ files register theirs).
53	# Format is ``module.entity.action`` per STRUCTURE §7.
54	ADMIN_USER_MANAGE = "admin.user.manage"
55	ADMIN_ROLE_MANAGE = "admin.role.manage"
56	ADMIN_AUDIT_READ = "admin.audit.read"
57	ADMIN_TENANT_MANAGE = "admin.tenant.manage"
58	CORE_DOCUMENT_READ = "core.document.read"
59	CORE_SETTING_MANAGE = "core.setting.manage"
60	
61	register_permissions(
62	    ADMIN_USER_MANAGE,
63	    ADMIN_ROLE_MANAGE,
64	    ADMIN_AUDIT_READ,
65	    ADMIN_TENANT_MANAGE,
66	    CORE_DOCUMENT_READ,
67	    CORE_SETTING_MANAGE,
68	    descriptions={
69	        ADMIN_USER_MANAGE: "Create, edit and deactivate users",
70	        ADMIN_ROLE_MANAGE: "Create roles and assign permissions",
71	        ADMIN_AUDIT_READ: "Read the audit log",
72	        ADMIN_TENANT_MANAGE: "Manage tenant settings and provisioning",
73	        CORE_DOCUMENT_READ: "View documents and their flow",
74	        CORE_SETTING_MANAGE: "Manage tenant-level configuration",
75	    },
76	)
77	
78	
79	async def sync_permission_catalog(session: AsyncSession) -> int:
80	    """Upsert every code-declared key into core_permissions (D-009). Idempotent: existing
81	    keys are left as-is, only missing ones are inserted, so re-running creates no dupes.
82	    Permissions are GLOBAL data — callers run this under system_context (seed/provisioning).
83	    Returns the number of rows inserted this call."""
84	    existing = set(
85	        (await session.execute(select(Permission.key))).scalars().all()
86	    )
87	    inserted = 0
88	    for key, description in _CATALOG.items():
89	        if key in existing:
90	            continue
91	        session.add(Permission(key=key, description=description))
92	        inserted += 1
93	    await session.flush()
94	    return inserted
95	
96	
97	# --- Permission resolution + TTL cache (D-009) --------------------------------
98	
99	_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS = 60.0
100	# key -> (expires_at_monotonic, permissions). Process-local; multi-worker deploys lag
101	# per worker by at most the TTL, or instantly on token_version bump (the key changes).
102	_CACHE: dict[tuple[uuid.UUID, uuid.UUID, int], tuple[float, frozenset[str]]] = {}
103	
104	
105	def clear_cache() -> None:
106	    """Drop every cached resolution. Used by tests and a future global flush."""
107	    _CACHE.clear()
108	
109	
110	def invalidate(tenant_id: uuid.UUID, user_id: uuid.UUID, token_version: int) -> None:
111	    """Evict one principal's cached permissions after a role change (D-009). Callers that
112	    only know (tenant, user) can pass any token_version they hold; on mismatch the stale
113	    entry simply expires within the TTL — but admin role mutations should pass the live
114	    token_version so the next request recomputes immediately."""
115	    _CACHE.pop((tenant_id, user_id, token_version), None)
116	
117	
118	async def _query_permissions(
119	    session: AsyncSession, user_id: uuid.UUID, tenant_id: uuid.UUID
120	) -> frozenset[str]:
121	    """ONE join: user_roles -> role_permissions -> permissions -> effective key set.
122	    Runs under the request's tenant context, so the user_roles/role_permissions rows are
123	    already tenant-filtered; the explicit user_id predicate narrows to this principal."""
124	    stmt = (
125	        select(Permission.key)
126	        .select_from(UserRole)
127	        .join(RolePermission, RolePermission.role_id == UserRole.role_id)
128	        .join(Permission, Permission.id == RolePermission.permission_id)
129	        .where(UserRole.user_id == user_id)
130	        .distinct()
131	    )
132	    keys = (await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all()
133	    return frozenset(keys)
134	
135	
136	async def resolve_permissions(
137	    session: AsyncSession,
138	    user_id: uuid.UUID,
139	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
140	    token_version: int,
141	    now: float | None = None,
142	) -> frozenset[str]:
143	    """Effective permission set for a principal, memoized 60s (D-009). ``now`` is an
144	    optional monotonic timestamp for deterministic tests; production uses time.monotonic.
145	    Tests prefer clear_cache()/invalidate() over advancing the clock."""
146	    clock = now if now is not None else time.monotonic()
147	    cache_key = (tenant_id, user_id, token_version)
148	    cached = _CACHE.get(cache_key)
149	    if cached is not None and cached[0] > clock:
150	        return cached[1]
151	    permissions = await _query_permissions(session, user_id, tenant_id)
152	    _CACHE[cache_key] = (clock + _CACHE_TTL_SECONDS, permissions)
153	    return permissions
154	
155	
156	# --- require_permission dependency factory (D-009) ----------------------------
157	
158	
159	def require_permission(key: str) -> Callable[..., Awaitable[Any]]:
160	    """FastAPI dependency factory: returns a dependency that loads the current principal
161	    (reusing get_current_user) and raises PermissionDeniedError (403, code
162	    ``rbac.permission_denied``, details naming the missing key) unless ``key`` is in the
163	    principal's resolved permissions. Attach per route via
164	    ``dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(ADMIN_USER_MANAGE))]``."""
165	
166	    # Imported here, not at module top, to avoid a core import cycle: deps imports rbac
167	    # (get_current_user resolves permissions) and rbac imports deps (this guard).
168	    from app.core.deps import CurrentUser, get_current_user
169	
170	    async def _dependency(
171	        current: Annotated[CurrentUser, Depends(get_current_user)],
172	    ) -> CurrentUser:
173	        if key not in current.permissions:
174	            raise PermissionDeniedError(
175	                code="rbac.permission_denied",
176	                message=f"Missing permission: {key}",
177	                details={"permission": key},
178	            )
179	        return current
180	
181	    return _dependency
182	
183	
184	# --- Field-level read masking (D-009) -----------------------------------------
185	
186	# Serialization-time principal permissions. Set by get_current_user per request and by
187	# the test ``permissions_context`` fixture; default empty so anything serialized OUTSIDE
188	# a request (jobs, tests without the fixture) fails CLOSED — masked fields read as None.
189	current_permissions: ContextVar[frozenset[str]] = ContextVar(
190	    "current_permissions", default=frozenset()
191	)
192	
193	def _mask_serializer(
194	    permission: str, value: Any, handler: SerializerFunctionWrapHandler
195	) -> Any:
196	    """WrapSerializer body (D-009): emit the real serialized value only when the guarding
197	    permission is present in current_permissions, else None. The permission is bound via
198	    functools.partial below — a WrapSerializer cannot read loose Annotated metadata."""
199	    if permission in current_permissions.get():
200	        return handler(value)
201	    return None
202	
203	
204	def Masked[T](tp: type[T], permission: str) -> Any:  # noqa: N802 - type-factory, PascalCase by design
205	    """Annotate a Pydantic field as read-masked behind ``permission`` (D-009).
206	
207	    Usage::
208	
209	        class EmployeeRead(ApiModel):
210	            base_salary: Masked(Decimal | None, "hr.compensation.read")
211	
212	    Serializes to the real value when current_permissions contains the key, else None.
213	    CONVENTION: masked fields are EXCLUDED from the entity's Create/Update schemas and
214	    edited through a separate permission-guarded endpoint, so a partial update can never
215	    silently null a masked field (the HR module enforces this for compensation)."""
216	    return Annotated[
217	        tp | None,
218	        WrapSerializer(functools.partial(_mask_serializer, permission)),
219	    ]

51	def _uuid_text(sql: str, **params: object):
52	    """A raw ``text()`` statement whose listed UUID params bind through ``sa.Uuid`` so a uuid.UUID
53	    value adapts to each engine's storage (32-char hex on SQLite, native uuid on PG) — a bare
54	    aiosqlite bind of a UUID object is unsupported."""
55	    typed = [
56	        sa.bindparam(key, value=value, type_=sa.Uuid)
57	        if isinstance(value, uuid.UUID)
58	        else sa.bindparam(key, value=value)
59	        for key, value in params.items()
60	    ]

1	# Finance (`backend/app/modules/finance/`)
2	
3	Finance is the first business module and the **bottom of the dependency order** (STRUCTURE §5):
4	every other module may read `finance/queries.py`, and finance imports no other module. The
5	full normative design lives in [docs/architecture.md](../architecture.md) (D-017…D-022); this
6	guide is the operator/contributor map, and it grows with each finance task (PLAN 4.1…4.10).
7	
8	## Status
9	
10	PLAN 4.1 laid the **schema foundation**: the chart of accounts and fiscal years/periods.
11	PLAN 4.2 (this task) adds the **universal journal** (D-017) — the heart of the system — and the
12	**four DB-level guard triggers** (D-018/D-017). AP/AR, payments and FX land in PLAN 4.3…4.10.
13	
14	| File | Concern | Key decision |
15	|---|---|---|
16	| `constants.py` | account/period enums + the normal-balance mapping; `EntryStatus`, `DocumentType`; permission keys (incl. `finance.journal.read/post/reverse`) | D-021, D-018, D-017, D-009 |
17	| `models/accounts.py` | `Account`, `AccountGroup`, `FiscalYear`, `FiscalPeriod` | D-021, D-018 |
18	| `models/journal.py` | `JournalEntry`, `JournalLine` (the universal journal) | D-017, D-021 |
19	| `schemas.py` | Create/Update/Read/Filter + journal entry/line schemas | — |
20	| `service/accounts.py` | chart-of-accounts business logic | D-021 |
21	| `service/periods.py` | fiscal years/periods + open/close lifecycle | D-018 |
22	| `service/journal.py` | draft creation, two-flush posting, reversal | D-017 |
23	| `events.py` | `JournalEntryPosted`, `JournalEntryReversed` | D-011 |
24	| `queries.py` | the cross-module read interface finance **exposes** | STRUCTURE §5 |
25	| `router.py` | thin HTTP layer at `/api/v1/finance` | D-013 (idempotent post/reverse) |
26	
27	> Money/quantity/rate exactness comes from `core/money.py` (D-015): `MoneyType`/`QuantityType`
28	> store NUMERIC on Postgres and INTEGER scaled minor units on SQLite, so the balance trigger's
29	> SUM and the one-side CHECK are exact on **both** engines; `allocate()` is the largest-remainder
30	> splitter (FX residual-cent, tax/discount splits).
31	
32	## The chart of accounts — why statements become derivable (D-021)
33	
34	Atlas follows the S/4HANA "universal journal" rule: every financial statement is a **projection**
35	of journal lines, never a separately-stored total. For that to work, each account carries the
36	minimal metadata from which all four statements derive mechanically:
37	
38	- **`account_type`** — one of `ASSET`, `LIABILITY`, `EQUITY`, `REVENUE`, `EXPENSE`. This single
39	  field drives every statement: the trial balance groups by account; the P&L sums
40	  `REVENUE` + `EXPENSE` over a range; the balance sheet takes `ASSET` / `LIABILITY` / `EQUITY`
41	  cumulative to a date (with retained earnings computed on the fly from `REVENUE` + `EXPENSE`
42	  net over all history).
43	- **`normal_balance`** (`DEBIT` / `CREDIT`) — derivable from the type (`ASSET`/`EXPENSE` → `DEBIT`;
44	  `LIABILITY`/`EQUITY`/`REVENUE` → `CREDIT`) but **stored** for query simplicity. The service
45	  defaults it from the type when a caller omits it, so the stored side can never disagree with
46	  the type.
47	- **`cash_flow_category`** (`OPERATING` / `INVESTING` / `FINANCING`, nullable) and
48	  **`is_cash_equivalent`** — feed the indirect cash-flow statement.
49	- **`is_postable`** — only leaf/postable accounts accept journal lines; presentation roll-up
50	  accounts carry no postings. The journal posting service (4.2) enforces this on every line.
51	
52	The **account-group tree** (`fin_account_groups`, self-referential `parent_id`) is a **pure
53	presentation hierarchy** — it carries no postings and no balances; accounts hang off a group via
54	`account_group_id`. Because the hierarchy lives entirely on the group tree, accounts themselves
55	have no `parent_id`. The service guards the tree against cycles (a group can never be its own
56	ancestor) when a group is reparented.
57	
58	The account-type model implemented here is **exactly** what the statement projections in 4.x
59	consume — no statement code needs anything beyond these fields.
60	
61	## Fiscal periods and the close lifecycle (D-018)
62	
63	A **`FiscalYear`** owns N **`FiscalPeriod`** rows. Creating a year auto-generates `period_count`
64	(default 12) **contiguous, non-overlapping monthly periods**: each period runs from its start to
65	the day before the next period's start, so the periods exactly tile the year — and the year's
66	`end_date` is set to the last period's end. Month lengths are handled correctly (a January 31st
67	start clamps February to the 28th/29th).
68	
69	Every period and year starts `OPEN`. The lifecycle:
70	
71	- **`close_period`** sets a period `CLOSED`; **`open_period`** reopens it (refused if the period's
72	  year is already `CLOSED`).
73	- **`close_fiscal_year`** is allowed only once **every** one of its periods is `CLOSED` — a closed
74	  year asserts the whole year is settled.
75	
76	A `CLOSED` period rejects postings dated within it. The **date → period lookup** the journal uses
77	on every posting is backed by the `(tenant_id, start_date, end_date)` index and exposed as
78	`queries.find_period_for_date`.
79	
80	### The close-time invariant (D-018, now enforced)
81	
82	D-018 mandates period-close enforcement at **both** the service and DB level.
83	
84	- **`service/periods.assert_period_closable(...)`** now refuses closing a period that is already
85	  closed **or** that still holds `DRAFT` journal entries dated within it (a draft in a closed
86	  period would become unpostable). Posted/reversed entries are immutable settled facts and never
87	  block a close.
88	- The **DB-level period-posting trigger** `trg_fin_journal_entries_period_open_*` fires on
89	  `fin_journal_entries` (migration `0009`) on a direct posted INSERT and on the DRAFT→POSTED
90	  UPDATE; it **re-derives** the open period from `NEW.posting_date` by date, so a wrong
91	  `fiscal_period_id` can never smuggle a posting into a closed period. It raises
92	  `ATLAS_PERIOD_CLOSED` → `finance.period_closed` (422).
93	
94	## The universal journal (D-017)
95	
96	One append-only line table (`fin_journal_lines`) is the single source of truth for every FI/CO
97	view (D-021); `fin_journal_entries` is the header carrying entry-level lifecycle. An entry is
98	**single-transaction-currency**. For v1 functional amounts **equal** transaction amounts (single
99	functional currency; posting-time FX translation lands in 4.3).
100	
101	**Lifecycle:** `DRAFT` → `POSTED` → `REVERSED`. A posted entry is **immutable**; the only
102	correction is a reversing entry (CLAUDE.md rule 8). Numbers (`JE-YYYY-#####`) are **gapless** and
103	claimed at **posting**, never at draft creation (D-012), so an abandoned draft burns no number.
104	
105	### Posting protocol — two flushes (D-017)
106	
107	`service/journal.post_entry` is deliberately two-flush because the unit of work does not guarantee
108	cross-table UPDATE order:
109	
110	1. Validate the entry is `DRAFT`, has ≥2 one-sided lines that balance, and that `posting_date`
111	   falls in an **open** period (422 `finance.period_closed` before touching the DB).
112	2. Claim the gapless `entry_number` in **this** transaction.
113	3. **Flush 1** — set each *loaded* line's `is_posted`/`posting_date`/`fiscal_period_id` while the
114	   entry is still `DRAFT` (the line-immutability trigger keys on `OLD.is_posted = FALSE`, so the
115	   posting flush is allowed).
116	4. **Flush 2** — set the header `POSTED`/`posted_at`/`fiscal_period_id` (the period + balance
117	   triggers fire on this DRAFT→POSTED UPDATE).
118	5. Publish `JournalEntryPosted`; commit via `run_in_uow`.
119	
120	Lines are mutated as **loaded objects** (never bulk `update()`) so the audit diffs are captured
121	and the audit bulk-write assertion is respected. The denormalized line fields make every
122	statement projection a header-join-free query over `fin_journal_lines` (D-021).
123	
124	### Reversal-only correction (D-017)
125	
126	`service/journal.reverse_entry` loads a `POSTED` entry, creates a **new** entry of the same
127	`document_type` with each line's debit/credit **swapped** in both currency pairs, posts it (its
128	own number), then sets the original `REVERSED` + `reversed_by_entry_id` — the **only** mutation
129	the immutability trigger permits on a posted header. The two documents are linked in docflow with
130	link type `reverses`. No deletes, no in-place edits, ever.
131	
132	### The four DB-guard triggers (migration 0009, both dialects)
133	
134	| Trigger | Table / event | Raises | Enforces |
135	|---|---|---|---|
136	| `trg_fin_journal_entries_period_open_ins` / `_upd` | entries, BEFORE INSERT / UPDATE (DRAFT→POSTED) | `ATLAS_PERIOD_CLOSED` | posting only into an open period covering `posting_date` (D-018) |
137	| `trg_fin_journal_entries_balanced` | entries, BEFORE UPDATE (DRAFT→POSTED) | `ATLAS_UNBALANCED_ENTRY` | Σ functional debit = Σ functional credit > 0 over the lines (D-017) |
138	| `trg_fin_journal_entries_immutable` / `_no_delete` | entries, BEFORE UPDATE / DELETE on a POSTED header | `ATLAS_POSTED_IMMUTABLE` | a posted entry is immutable except the sanctioned POSTED→REVERSED transition (D-017) |
139	| `trg_fin_journal_lines_immutable` / `_no_delete` | lines, BEFORE UPDATE / DELETE where `OLD.is_posted` | `ATLAS_POSTED_IMMUTABLE` | a posted line is frozen; the posting flush (FALSE→TRUE) is allowed (D-017) |
140	
141	Plus the column CHECK `ck_fin_journal_lines_one_side` (debit XOR credit per line). The triggers
142	are written per-dialect (plpgsql on Postgres, `RAISE(ABORT)` on SQLite) and proven firing on
143	**both** engines by `tests/modules/finance/test_journal_db_guards.py` (raw-SQL bypass, the default
144	SQLite run + the `-m pg` Postgres run). Tokens are translated to the error envelope by
145	`core/exceptions.py` (`finance.period_closed`/`finance.journal_unbalanced`/`finance.entry_immutable`,
146	all 422).
147	
148	## The `queries.py` contract (what other modules read)
149	
150	Finance exposes exactly three stable read functions (STRUCTURE §5 — everyone may import these):
151	
152	- `find_period_for_date(session, tenant_id, on_date) -> FiscalPeriod | None`
153	- `get_period_status(session, tenant_id, on_date) -> PeriodStatus | None`
154	- `account_exists(session, tenant_id, code) -> bool`
155	
156	Inventory and sales call `get_period_status` to refuse stock/sales documents dated into a closed
157	period before they reach the GL; the journal calls `find_period_for_date` to resolve an entry's
158	period from its posting date.
159	
160	## Permissions (D-009)
161	
162	| Key | Guards |
163	|---|---|
164	| `finance.account.read` | read accounts and account groups |
165	| `finance.account.manage` | create/edit accounts and account groups |
166	| `finance.period.read` | read fiscal years and periods |
167	| `finance.period.manage` | create fiscal years, open/close periods |
168	| `finance.journal.read` | read journal entries and their lines |
169	| `finance.journal.post` | create draft entries **and** post them |
170	| `finance.journal.reverse` | reverse posted entries |
171	
172	AP, AR and payment keys are registered by their own tasks (4.3+).
173	
174	## API (`/api/v1/finance`)
175	
176	- `GET/POST /accounts`, `GET/PATCH /accounts/{id}` — list uses cursor pagination + the `Page`
177	  envelope; filters (`account_type`, `is_postable`, `is_active`, `account_group_id`) fold into
178	  the cursor fingerprint.
179	- `GET/POST /account-groups`
180	- `GET/POST /fiscal-years` (POST generates the periods), `GET /fiscal-periods`
181	- `POST /fiscal-periods/{id}/close` and `/open` — action sub-resources (STRUCTURE §7), guarded by
182	  `finance.period.manage`.
183	- `POST /journal-entries` (create draft), `GET /journal-entries` (paginated), `GET /{id}` (with
184	  lines) — `finance.journal.post` / `finance.journal.read`.
185	- `POST /journal-entries/{id}/post` and `/{id}/reverse` — action sub-resources, **idempotent**
186	  (D-013, require the `Idempotency-Key` header), guarded by `finance.journal.post` /
187	  `finance.journal.reverse`.
188	
189	Writes commit through `run_in_uow` (D-011), so audit rows ride the same transaction and the
190	event semantics will be identical to seed/CLI once finance publishes events.
191

189	def publish(session: AsyncSession, event: DomainEvent) -> None:
190	    """Convenience free function delegating to the active bus, so callers can
191	    ``from app.core.events import publish`` without reaching for the singleton."""
192	    bus.publish(session, event)
193	
194	
195	async def _drain_and_dispatch(session: AsyncSession) -> None:
196	    """Pop buffered events FIFO and run their handlers, sharing ``session``. Handlers may
197	    publish more events (appended to the same buffer); we keep draining breadth-first up to
198	    MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW total dispatches, then raise EventCycleError. A handler raising
199	    propagates — run_in_uow's caller rolls the whole transaction back (D-011: no isolation).
200	    """
201	    buffer = _buffer(session)
202	    dispatched = 0
203	    while buffer:
204	        event = buffer.pop(0)  # FIFO: oldest first
205	        for handler in handlers_for(event.key):
206	            if dispatched >= MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW:
207	                raise EventCycleError(dispatched)
208	            await handler(session, event)
209	            dispatched += 1
210	    # Defensive: an event with no handler still counts toward nothing; a cap breach can
211	    # only happen above. Clearing the (now empty) key keeps session.info tidy.
212	    session.info.pop(_BUFFER_KEY, None)
213	
214	
215	async def run_in_uow(
216	    session: AsyncSession,
217	    work: Callable[[], Awaitable[None]] | Awaitable[None],
218	) -> None:
219	    """The single sanctioned unit-of-work helper (D-011). Used by the request session
220	    dependency (core/deps), by seed.py and by CLI flows, so HTTP, seed and tests get
221	    IDENTICAL event semantics.
222	
223	    Sequence: run ``work`` (the business mutation that publishes events) -> drain the
224	    buffered events FIFO and run their handlers on the SAME session (so handler effects,
225	    e.g. a COGS journal, are in the same transaction as the trigger, e.g. the stock
226	    issue) -> commit. If the business work OR any handler raises (or the cascade cap is
227	    hit), roll the WHOLE transaction back and re-raise — the trigger's own writes do not
228	    persist. Handlers run under the trigger's active tenant context (D-007); nothing here
229	    changes it.
230	
231	    ``work`` may be a coroutine object or a zero-arg callable returning an awaitable, so
232	    both ``run_in_uow(session, service_coro)`` and ``run_in_uow(session, lambda: ...)``
233	    read naturally at call sites.
234	    """
235	    try:
236	        awaitable = work() if callable(work) else work
237	        await awaitable
238	        await _drain_and_dispatch(session)
239	        await session.commit()
240	    except Exception:
241	        await session.rollback()
242	        # Drop any partially drained / leftover buffer so the next uow on this session
243	        # (tests reuse one session) starts clean.
244	        session.info.pop(_BUFFER_KEY, None)
245	        raise
